questions.prompt: Your phone is lost. Which call protects your money first?

options.text: Your bank's 24×7 helpline, to block UPI and cards
A friend, to tell them the news
options.explanationWrong: A friend cannot block your accounts. Call your bank first.

options.text: The number in a 'found your phone' message
options.explanationWrong: That message is likely a trap. Never rely on contacts from a suspicious message.
Waiting gives a thief more time. Act quickly.

questions.explanationCorrect: Banks have 24×7 helplines. Block UPI and cards first, because that is where your money is.

questions.prompt: Which number is the national cybercrime helpline?

options.explanationWrong: That is not the cybercrime helpline.
That is not the cybercrime helpline.
That is not the cybercrime helpline.

questions.explanationCorrect: The national cybercrime helpline is 1930. Save it in your phone and your family's phones.

questions.prompt: Where can you report cyber fraud online?

options.text: A website from a search advert that looks official
options.explanationWrong: Adverts can be fake. Type the official address yourself.
Social media is not an official reporting route.
Reports create a record and can help you and others.

questions.explanationCorrect: The national portal is cybercrime.gov.in. You can also call 1930.
